title: Ledger
description: The completeness record of a review, of which there is one: one row per rule probed, naming what was opened and the verdict reached. Each probe writes its rows to the file its instructions name; the reporting script reads those files, never what a probe says when it returns, and merges them into the one ledger that travels with the review. A row is complete only with its examined and evidence filled; a statement that a rule was considered is not a row

rows.evidence: Both scripts run under set -euo pipefail, and no step is wrapped in a construct that would let the script continue.
scripts/verify.sh:21 pipes the check into tail, so its status is lost.

violations.observation: Losing the check's exit status in a pipe into tail

rows.evidence: The change adds one check to a script and introduces no domain concept that could be left implicit.

headCommit.description: The commit every row was reached against

rows.description: One row per rule probed: the rows of each probe in the order of its instructions

Row.description: One probe's result on one rule: a rule of ours, or a rule of a ruleset from outside ours

RuleRow.description: The verdict reached on one of our rules

rule.description: The rule probed, referenced by its id

BookRow.description: The verdict the escalation probe reached on one rule of the ruleset it selected

BookRule.description: A rule from outside ours, referenced by where it is read: the reporting script renders the link, the probe writes none into its observation

RulesetUrl.description: Where the selected ruleset was read: its canonical URL from the index

BookRuleHeading.description: The heading of a rule in its ruleset

Verdict.description: What a probe reached on one rule; the verdict decides what else is carried

Violated.description: The rule is violated: evidence names file and line inside the surface, and every finding is carried as a violation

Clean.description: The rule holds: evidence names what was checked that would have exposed a violation; it carries no violations

NotApplicable.description: The rule cannot apply to what is under review: evidence says why. No findings is not a reason; it carries no violations

Examined.description: What was actually opened to reach the verdict. Context the probe needed and was not handed is named here rather than silently dropped

ExaminedItem.description: One thing opened to reach the verdict: a file, a symbol, a call site, a test file including the case where none exists, or a search with its query

Evidence.description: What the verdict rests on; the verdict it sits in says what it has to name
